as_told.title: Major Mansmann tracked down, admits supervising Jacobs

plain: After his 1964 UFO sighting at Vandenberg Air Force Base, Bob Jacobs says the Air Force denied he had ever served, and someone blew up his mailbox. At the time he was a photo instrumentation specialist, someone who filmed tests at the base. Jacobs says one inquiry was told there was never a Robert Jacobs in the Air Force, and another that there was never one at Vandenberg. He points to his DD214, the military discharge record, and his officer efficiency reports, his performance reviews, as proof he was there. He also says that one night he and his wife came home from a movie and a voice on the phone said 'fireworks in your mailbox at night, oh what a beautiful sight, you're going down,' and then his mailbox blew up. The researcher Robert Hastings, who studies UFOs at nuclear bases, repeats the same account. Michels adds that Jacobs had managed over 130 people. He says Hastings and other researchers tracked down his former superior, Major Florenze Mansmann, who admitted in the 1990s that Jacobs had worked under him. Told this way, it shows how hard the military pushed back on someone who spoke about what he saw.
